queries.query: robotic ultrasound scanning finite area sliding soft contact model force torque impedance control
queries.purpose: Attempt to falsify the claim that the scalar normal Hunt-Crossley environment representation is insufficient for force- and trajectory-relevant sliding ultrasound contact by locating direct models and experiments that already close the finite-area, tangential-force, and contact-moment gap.
queries.expected_close_condition: Identify direct robotic-ultrasound evidence showing whether finite-area geometry, sliding resistance, or contact moment materially changes force regulation or scanning behavior, or conclude that the claimed phenomenon lacks decision-grade support.
queries.lead_statement: For continuous robotic ultrasound scanning, extending NNBO beyond a scalar normal Hunt-Crossley environment may be necessary because finite-area sliding, changing surface geometry, tangential resistance, and contact moment can alter the impedance decision and its safety/performance boundary.
